title: Prorated Variant Rollout — Billing & Consumption Playbook
author: Priya Nair
body:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines the billing and consumption rules, engineering and finance handoffs, and operational runbook for proration during model variant rollouts. It covers: pricing transitions when customers migrate traffic between variants (e.g., high-fidelity -> quantized), temporary dual-crediting during canaries, and automated reconciliation for monthly invoices. The intent is to keep customer costs predictable, preserve accounting integrity, and enable safe staged rollouts of new model variants without surprise charges.

Goals
-----
- Ensure transparent, auditable billing when per-token cost changes due to variant rollouts.
- Minimize customer-facing bill surprises during staged canaries and partial migrations.
- Provide a repeatable, automated reconciliation pipeline (engineering + finance) for proration.
- Define thresholds and SLOs for telemetry and alerts tied to billing impact.

Scope
-----
Includes: hosted API customers, Dedicated reserved pools with metered overage, and Hybrid customers with mixed-hosted/dedicated consumption.
Excludes: Marketplace billing reconciliation for third-party resellers (handled by commerce).

Key definitions
---------------
- Variant: A model binary or configuration (quantized, pruned, larger model) served under a catalog SKU.
- Effective unit price (EUP): the per-token (or per-embedding) price applied for a given request.
- Dual-credit window: a bounded timeframe where both source and destination variants are credited for a single request to avoid double-billing or under-billing during rollout.
- Migration event: an orchestrated update that moves a customer or route from variant A -> variant B.

Principles
----------
1. Transparent: customers should be able to simulate expected cost change before rollout.
2. Reversible: safe rollback path that leaves billing state consistent.
3. Low-latency reconciliation: any proration mismatches must be resolved within the billing period (<= 7 days post-cycle).
4. Minimal manual steps: automation preferred; manual escapes need explicit approvals.

High-level approach
-------------------
- Preflight: calculate estimated delta across historical consumption (7/30/90 day windows). Provide a preflight report via Console and API.
- Controlled rollout: Canary (1–5%), Ramp (5–50%), Full (50–100%) with configurable windows. During Canary and Ramp stages, apply dual-crediting for affected requests to ensure no customer unexpectedly overpays.
- Reconciliation: At the end of the billing window, generate a prorated invoice adjustment for variant EUP differences.

Billing rules (concise)
----------------------
1. When a request is served by variant B but the contract/route is still priced for variant A, apply the following precedence:
   a. If customer has opted into automatic variant-billing migration, charge EUP_B immediately.
   b. If customer has not opted in and the rollout is within the dual-credit window, charge the lower of EUP_A and EUP_B up-front and record a pending adjustment for reconciliation.
   c. After reconciliation window closes, apply final charge equal to actual consumption priced at the signed contract EUP unless customer accepted new pricing.
2. Dual-credit window defaults: 72 hours for canary, 7 days for ramp. These are configurable per-customer.
3. For Reserved Dedicated customers with committed usage, delta is applied to overage buckets only; committed units are counted against original committed EUP unless a contract amendment is processed.

Proration examples
------------------
Example 1: Simple hosted customer
- Contract: variant-A priced at $0.0009/token.
- Rollout: after canary, 10,000 tokens served by variant-B priced at $0.0006/token during a 24-hour canary.
- Up-front charge (per rule 1b): min(0.0009,0.0006) => $0.0006/token x 10,000 = $6.00 charged.
- End-of-period reconciliation: since contract not updated, final charge uses contract EUP $0.0009/token => difference = (0.0009-0.0006)*10,000 = $3.00 additional charge or credit depending on rule selection. The system will prefer a single final charge and show line items: canary partial charge ($6.00), reconciliation delta ($3.00).

Example 2: Dedicated reserved customer
- Committed units: 10M tokens/month at $0.0005/token (applies to committed).
- During a ramp, 1M tokens are served by variant-B at $0.0004/token (lower).
- No change to committed allocation; overage delta is 0 because consumption is within commitment. If variant-B is more expensive, overage would be billed at overage EUP and reconciled.

Preflight report fields (Console + API)
-------------------------------------
- Historical token counts (7/30/90 days) per-route and per-tenant.
- Estimated monthly delta: absolute $ and percent.
- Risk score: low/medium/high based on delta magnitude and customer churn sensitivity.
- Recommended rollout cadence (recommended canary %, ramp %, window).

Sample Preflight API response (pseudo-JSON shown as text)
--------------------------------------------------------
{
  "customer_id": "acct_123",
  "7d_tokens": "1,200,000",
  "estimated_delta_monthly_usd": "$420",
  "recommended_canary_pct": "2%",
  "risk_score": "medium"
}

Operational runbook: rollout (engineering + growth)
--------------------------------------------------
1) Prep (Owner: Product / Solutions)
   - Run preflight for target customer and route; attach results to the rollout ticket.
   - Confirm customer communication plan (email + Console notice).
2) Canary (Owner: Platform Eng)
   - Enable variant routing for N% of traffic via routing policy.
   - Enable dual-crediting mode in billing service.
   - Monitor: cost delta, latency, client error rate. Alert on >10% unexpected cost delta or >2x error rate.
3) Ramp (Owner: Platform Eng -> Customer Success)
   - Increment percent in steps (5%, 15%, 50%) with at least 24h between steps.
   - If customer has approved price migration, move to immediate EUP_B charge (no pending reconciliation).
4) Finalize (Owner: Finance + Billing)
   - End dual-crediting. Run reconciler job to compute final invoice adjustments.
   - Communicate invoice changes in Console and email.

Reconciliation process (Finance pipeline)
---------------------------------------
1. Invoices generator aggregates per-request recorded EUPs and pending adjustments.
2. Reconciler job consolidates dual-credit entries, applies contract rules, and produces adjustment lines.
3. Adjustments older than 7 days must be resolved in the next billing cycle; manual review if unresolved.
4. SLO: 95% of reconciliation adjustments auto-resolved; <5% escalate to Finance for manual intervention.

Alerts and telemetry (SLOs and thresholds)
-----------------------------------------
- Billing Impact Alert: triggers when estimated monthly delta for a customer exceeds $1,000 or 15% of prior monthly invoice (whichever is lower).
- Reconciliation Backlog Alert: triggers when >48 hours of pending adjustments exist at >1,000 items.
- Accuracy SLO: billing mismatch rate <= 0.03% of total billed amount per month.

Permissions and approvals
------------------------
- Any non-automated proration override requires approval from Finance (billing lead) and Product (owner).
- Contract amendments (change committed EUP) must be recorded in CRM and linked to the billing ticket.

Compatibility table (variant billing behaviors)
---------------------------------------------
| Variant type       | Default proration | Dual-credit window | Notes |
|--------------------|-------------------:|-------------------:|-------|
| Quantized (vQ)     | lower-price-first  | 72h                | Best for opt-in auto-migrations |
| Fused Large (vL)   | charge-new-immediately | 24h           | High-cost impact; default requires customer opt-in |
| Adaptive-quality   | prorate by percentile | 7d             | Complex; use preflight simulation |

Customer communication templates
--------------------------------
- Canary notification: short message describing expected changes, instructions to opt-out, link to preflight report.
- Invoice adjustment notification: detailed line-item breakdown with reconciler justification and support contact.

CLI / Admin examples
--------------------
- Start canary for acct_123 on route /api/generate at 2%:
  redwoodctl rollout start --acct acct_123 --route /api/generate --variant vB --percent 2 --dual-credit 72h
- Query pending adjustments:
  redwoodctl billing pending-adjustments --acct acct_123 --since 2027-02-01

Migration checklist (pre-rollout)
--------------------------------
1. Ticket created and preflight attached (Product).
2. Customer notified; opt-out window set to >=24h (CS).
3. Billing dual-crediting configured (Billing Platform Eng).
4. Monitoring dashboards and alerts are enabled (SRE/Platform).
5. Support runbook created and SLAs acknowledged (Support).

Rollback guidance
-----------------
1. If cost delta unacceptably increases (>30% or >$5k estimated monthly), immediately pause rollout and revert routing policy.
2. Disable dual-crediting and flag pending adjustments for manual audit.
3. Customer Success to notify customer and re-open opt-in flow where appropriate.

Metrics to capture post-rollout
------------------------------
- Actual vs estimated monthly delta (USD and percent).
- Number of invoices with adjustments and average adjustment size.
- Customer opt-outs and churn within 30 days.
- Reconciliation auto-resolution percentage.

FAQ (short)
-----------
Q: Will I be double-billed during canary?
A: No — dual-crediting ensures the system captures both candidate and source pricing information for reconciliation; customers see a clear line-item for adjustments.

Q: How long until adjustments appear on my invoice?
A: Adjustments are applied in the next invoice cycle but are visible in Console within 72 hours after the relevant dual-credit window closes.

Appendix: reconciliation pseudocode (conceptual)
------------------------------------------------
1. For each request r: record (tenant, timestamp, variant, tokens, EUP_recorded).
2. If dual-credit flagged: write pending_adjustment row with (tenant, request_id, EUP_source, EUP_dest, tokens).
3. At reconciliation job: for tenant t, sum tokens per EUP rule and apply contract precedence to produce final adjustment amount.

End of document.
